 Lubbock County election results delayed by machine error, ballot rescans 
 By Natalie Reyna Published : Nov. 4, 2026 at 8:43 PM CST | Updated : 47 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LUBBOCK, Texas (KCBD) - Elections Administrator Troy Havard says Lubbock County election results were delayed by a machine malfunction at one early voting location, required ballot rescans and a shortage of poll workers on Tuesday.
 Forty percent of registered voters in Lubbock County cast ballots during early voting.
 Machine malfunction at early voting site 
 Havard said a machine malfunction at one early voting location was the first sign of trouble. Election workers spotted the error on Oct. 22 and replaced the machine. Then the problem happened again at the same location.
 “At this point, I’m not even sure exactly how this happened,” Havard said.
 Havard said the law limits what his office can do with early voting ballots and the drives that hold the votes.
 “The law does not allow me to do anything with early voting until after Election Day begins and I can’t do anything with the drives that have the votes on them until after 7 p.m. on Election Day,” Havard said.
 His office had to make sure every vote from that location got counted.
 Ballot rescans and adjudication 
 “The easiest, most transparent, and most secure method of doing that was to rescan every single ballot from that early voting location so that we ensured every single vote was counted the way it was supposed to be,” Havard said. “That was 5,681 ballots and that took some time.”
 The Secretary of State’s Legal Division also told Havard’s office to rescan all 1,700 limited ballots cast during early voting. Each limited ballot consisted of two pieces of paper, front and back. The central count judge and an alternate judge had to adjudicate every one of those.
 “So, all of that added together led up to late results from Lubbock County,” Havard said. “But in the grand scheme of things, two things come out of that. Number one is that we know that we wanted to make sure we had accurate results no matter how long it took. And No. 2 is that our audit process works. We found an issue and we resolved that issue.”
 Poll worker shortage 
 Polls closed at 7 p.m., but some locations still had people in line. Those locations stayed open until about 9 p.m.
 Havard said some volunteers and an election worker quit before Election Day, and it became all hands on deck.
 “We were running really tight on poll workers for this election,” Havard said. “The parties did their part in trying to recruit as many people as they could, along with people in my office recruiting as many as they could.”
 Havard said that would result in longer lines at polling locations.
 Next election 
 The next big election in Texas is May 1 for cities and other local issues. People can sign up to help and get trained to work in that cycle by signing up here:
